skill.name: improve-ui
skill.description: Audit an existing product surface against its own design evidence, identify verified UI problems, and write self-contained implementation plans for another agent. Strictly read-only on product source. Use when asked to review, refine, improve, or clean up an interface without replacing its identity; investigate design-system drift; or prepare a design handoff.
skill.summary: Audit an existing interface against its governing design evidence and prepare implementation plans without changing product source.
skill.author: ibelick

content.user_title: Audit UI and Prepare Evidence-Based Design Plans
content.value_statement: Interface reviews can mistake intentional differences for defects and recommend changes without evidence. This skill verifies design findings and prepares selected implementation plans while preserving product identity.
actual_capabilities: Trace one product surface through routes, layouts, shared components, variants, tokens, and styles.
Identify current design documentation and prove which sources govern the selected surface.
Require a design contract, runtime connection, and one evidence-supported correction for every reported finding.
Recheck cited sources, remove contradicted findings, and report at most three supported issues.
Write self-contained plans for user-selected changes, covering reuse, affected consumers, validation, and stop conditions.
Reconcile existing plans against current source, documented decisions, affected surfaces, and status.
limitations: Does not implement fixes or modify product source; file edits are limited to design-plans/.
Does not install dependencies, run formatters, commit, or push changes.
Uses rendered evidence only when supplied or visual inspection is explicitly requested; perceptual judgments require rendered or user evidence.
Reports at most three findings and excludes accessibility, functional, and broader code-quality issues unless explicitly requested or otherwise in scope.

use_cases.title: Review a Product Surface
use_cases.description: Check a settings interface against its governing components and design decisions before proposing targeted visual changes.

use_cases.title: Investigate Design-System Drift
use_cases.description: Trace a dashboard through shared owners and resolved tokens to distinguish real inconsistencies from deliberate variants.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Implementation Handoff
use_cases.description: Turn an approved design finding into a self-contained plan with exact scope, reusable elements, validation, and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Use improve-ui to audit the account settings surface. Report supported UI findings and recommend one priority. Do not write plans or change product source.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: request a focused, read-only interface review.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Design Inconsistency
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit dashboard filter styling against current design guidance. Trace the governing variants and resolved tokens. Distinguish intentional exceptions from supported violations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: investigate a suspected design-system inconsistency.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Approved Correction
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a plan for the approved settings-label inconsistency. Recheck evidence, name exact reusable elements, and specify validation. Write only under design-plans/.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: hand an already selected change to an implementation agent.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile Existing Plans
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile existing design-plans/ files for the checkout surface against current source and accepted design decisions. Update stale evidence, scope, and status without implementing changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: refresh design handoffs after source or design decisions change.

output_examples.input: Audit settings when no candidate satisfies the evidence requirements.
output: Design language: audited surface, governing sources, documented decisions, owners, and explicit exceptions.
Findings: No supported findings were found.

output_examples.input: Prepare a plan for a selected and verified interface-copy correction.
output: Evidence chain: current commit, affected surface, observed contradiction, governing evidence, owner, and uncertainty.
Design decision: one supported correction with exact scope and reusable elements.
Changes: affected locations, intended edits, preserved behavior, and observable results.
Validation: product outcome, relevant interface states, system reuse, and repository checks.
Stop conditions and documentation: failed assumptions that halt implementation and decisions to record after acceptance.

best_practices: Specify one coherent surface and provide relevant design decisions or rendered evidence.
Select supported findings before requesting plans, and keep implementation separate from the audit.
Reconcile existing plans after source changes so implementation agents receive current evidence and scope.
anti_patterns: Requesting repository-wide visual normalization without proving shared runtime ownership or a binding design rule.
Treating repeated code, missing documentation, or personal preferences as sufficient evidence of a design defect.
Expecting direct fixes, dependency installation, or product-source edits from this planning-only skill.

faq.question: Does this skill implement UI changes?
faq.answer: No. It audits interfaces and writes selected implementation plans under design-plans/. Another agent executes those plans.

faq.question: Does the project need design documentation?
faq.answer: No. Missing documentation is not a finding. A direct contradiction in user-facing presentation or content can establish a design contract.

faq.question: How many findings does it report?
faq.answer: It reports at most three findings, ordered by confidence, user impact, reach, and correction cost.

faq.question: Will it inspect the rendered interface automatically?
faq.answer: No. Rendered evidence is used only when supplied or visual inspection is explicitly requested. Perceptual judgments require rendered or user evidence.

faq.question: Does the audit include accessibility and functional bugs?
faq.answer: Accessibility and HTML/ARIA findings require an explicit request. Functional bugs are excluded from design findings; request a separate functional review.

faq.question: Can it update an existing design plan?
faq.answer: Yes. When asked to reconcile, it rechecks current source and design decisions, then updates stale evidence, affected surfaces, and status.
